paper_title: Deciding Regular Games: a Playground for Exponential Time Algorithms
classifications: Theory of computation → Algorithmic game theory
Theory of computation → Logic and verification
statement: The algorithms presented in this work give rise to numerous questions that warrant further exploration. For instance, we know that explicitly given Muller games can be decided in polynomial time. Yet, we do not know if there are polynomial time algorithms that decide explicitly given McNaughton games. Another intriguing line of research is to investigate if there are exponential time algorithms p that decide colored Muller games when the parameter |C| ranges in the interval [ |V |, |V |/a], where a > 1. It could also be very interesting to replace the factor 2|V | with 2|W | in the running time that decides McNaughton games. If this can be done, then one implies that the ETH is not applicable to McNaughton games as opposed to colored Muller games and Rabin games. In addition, this work could be extended to dynamic settings or experimental studies, as in [17, 25]. Its dynamic programming-style approach may also inspire new advances, akin to DP-assisted methods in games on graphs [29, 30, 31]. These all may uncover new insights and lead to even more efficient algorithms.
